_meta.indication: PET imaging of patients with suspected prostate cancer recurrence and non-informative bone scintigraphy, CT or MRI, to help identify potential sites of recurrence for subsequent histologic confirmation; not a replacement for histologic verification.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Sponsor's retrospective study of Choline C 11 PET scans at the Mayo Clinic (plus a systematic review of four published studies supporting the 505(b)(2) application)
pivotal_trials.phase: Not a prospective phase trial; 505(b)(2) application based on a retrospective chart review and published literature
pivotal_trials.design: Retrospective chart review of men who underwent Choline C 11 PET to evaluate biochemical recurrence after failed initial treatment, supported by a systematic literature review of four studies comparing 11C-choline PET/CT to histopathology
pivotal_trials.population: Men with documented biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer after failed initial treatment (radical prostatectomy, radiotherapy, cryoablation, or androgen deprivation therapy)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: No prespecified primary endpoint (retrospective study); FDA characterized performance as the detection rate of recurrent lesions relative to a histopathology truth standard
pivotal_trials.n: 176 charts in the sponsor's retrospective study; four supporting studies (n=13, 15, 36, 34)
pivotal_trials.result: In the supporting studies, within each study at least half of patients with non-informative conventional imaging had positive 11C-choline PET/CT images and histologically verified recurrence (true positives: 11/13, 8/15, 23/36, 25/34). Sponsor's retrospective study reported sensitivity of 93% and specificity of 76% across all treatments, and sensitivity of 95% and specificity of 86% for prostatectomy patients.

key_safety: Exclusive of an uncommon, mild injection site reaction, no other adverse reactions have been reported. Only 1 adverse event (a mild, self-limiting injection site reaction) was described in the sponsor's retrospective review of 176 charts. Main theoretical risk is radiation exposure (effective dose 0.0161 rem/mCi).
target_moa: Radiolabeled analog of choline, a precursor for cell membrane phospholipid biosynthesis; increased phospholipid synthesis (increased choline uptake) is associated with cell proliferation and transformation in tumor cells, enabling PET visualization.
modality: radiopharmaceutical (positron-emitting C-11 labeled choline for PET imaging)

rems.type: There is no recommendation for Postmarket Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues warranting discussion.

basis.text: The application was designated Priority and reviewed under a priority review timeline.

citations.quote: This application was reviewed under a priority review time line but the review cycle was extended by a major amendment that prompted a clinical site inspection.

summary.text: Choline C 11 Injection (NDA 203-155) was a 505(b)(2) application submitted by the Mayo Clinic, received December 12, 2011, reviewed under priority review (cycle extended to a September 12, 2012 PDUFA date after a major amendment prompted a clinical site inspection), and approved on first cycle with no REMS and no postmarketing requirements or commitments; no advisory committee was convened.
